correctness_confidence.basis: All main theorems and lemmas hold after line-by-line verification of group identities, Cauchy-Davenport bounds, and p=3,5 edge cases. A minor expositional slip on p. 13 omits citing the active Lemma 4.1 bound m_1+c <= 2p-2 to exclude (p,p-1,p-1) at c=p-1.

rigor.basis: Arguments are generally careful and self-contained, handling boundary regimes (such as p=3, c=0, |S|=9 and p=5, L=3^6*2) explicitly. Minor polish issues include the omitted Lemma 4.1 citation on p. 13 and stating Lemma 2.2(b) without explicitly invoking it later.

novelty.basis: While building directly on Volkmann's exponential-coordinate order-value growth (Lemma 2.1) and Reiher's Property B, the three-set pigeonhole criterion on Z(G), heavy-line elimination, Property-B cross-splitting (Lemma 4.2), and fiber-doubled lifting for eta and s are original.

significance.basis: Lowers D(H_{p^3}) from 5p-4 to 4p-4 for all odd primes p>=3, strictly separating it from the Loewy length 4p-3, gives a conceptual proof of D(H_27)=8, and improves lower bounds for eta and s; however, the conjectured exact value 3p-1 and upper bounds for eta, s remain open.

reproducibility.basis: All mathematical proofs are explicit and verifiable from first principles modulo standard cited theorems (Reiher's Property B and Kemnitz theorems, Jennings' formula), complemented by explicit extremal witnesses and described Lean 4 core checks and Python DP verification.

summary: The manuscript investigates the large Davenport constant D(H_{p^3}) and short-subsequence invariants eta(H_{p^3}), s(H_{p^3}) for the Heisenberg group of order p^3 and odd prime exponent p. Building on symplectic exponential coordinates and Volkmann's order-value growth lemma, it introduces a three-set pigeonhole splitting criterion on Z(H_{p^3}), heavy-line elimination (Lemma 4.1), and a cross-splitting lemma using Reiher's Property B structure theorem (Lemma 4.2) to prove 3p-1 <= D(H_{p^3}) <= 4p-4 < 4p-3 = L(H_{p^3}) for all odd p >= 3. This settles D(H_27) = 8 conceptually and strictly separates D(H_{p^3}) from the Loewy length for all odd p. For p >= 5, Theorem 1.2 narrows the remaining [3p, 4p-4] gap to two explicit obstructions (O1)-(O2), and Theorem 1.3 proves eta(H_{p^3}) >= 7p-6 and s(H_{p^3}) >= 8p-7. All proofs check out mathematically, with one minor expositional omission on p. 13 in Case 3 (t=3) easily fixed by citing Lemma 4.1's m_1+c <= 2p-2.
strengths: Improves the uniform upper bound on D(H_{p^3}) from 5p-4 to 4p-4 for all odd primes p >= 3, strictly separating D(H_{p^3}) from the Loewy length 4p-3 = D_ord(H_{p^3}) in contrast to M_27.
Provides a purely conceptual, computer-free proof that D(H_27) = 8, carefully handling every p = 3, c = 0, |S| = 9 boundary case.

Constructs two explicit Aut(H_{p^3})-inequivalent minimal product-one sequences S^(1) and S^(2) of length 3p-1, and clean fiber-doubled witnesses T_eta and T_s establishing eta(H_{p^3}) >= 7p-6 and s(H_{p^3}) >= 8p-7.

Property-B cross-splitting (Lemma 4.2) and heavy-line elimination (Lemma 4.1) are technically clean and yield a concrete structural reduction of [3p, 4p-4] for p >= 5 to two explicit obstructions (O1)-(O2).
Transparently specifies the exact scope of the Lean 4.36.0 core formalization and Python DP checks without overclaiming mechanized coverage of the main theorems.
weaknesses: Does not resolve the conjectured exact value D(H_{p^3}) = 3p-1 for p >= 5, leaving a linear-width gap [3p-1, 4p-4] and the two structural obstructions (O1)-(O2) open.
Provides only lower bounds for eta(H_{p^3}) and s(H_{p^3}) with no upper bounds.

The residual class (O2) in Theorem 1.2 could be sharpened slightly near the upper endpoint 4p-4 (for instance, three-line triples at |S| = 4p-4 with reducible L_1 also split under the same argument used in Theorem 1.1).
Minor expositional issues: omitted invocation of Lemma 4.1 (m_1 + c <= 2p-2) on p. 13 when deducing m_1 = m_2 = p and c <= p-2, and stating Lemma 2.2(b) without explicitly invoking it later.
potential_errors: Page 13, Case 3 (t=3), second sub-bullet: The claim that m_3 <= m_2 <= m_1 <= p, m_1 + m_2 + m_3 + c >= 4p-3, and c <= p-1 force m_1 = m_2 = p, m_3 >= p-1, and c >= p-3 omits the solution (m_1, m_2, m_3, c) = (p, p-1, p-1, p-1). That configuration is already ruled out by Lemma 4.1's bound m_1 + c <= 2p-2 (stated at the start of Case 3 on p. 12), which forces c <= p-2 whenever m_1 = p, and is also ruled out by Lemma 2.2(a)+(c); citing m_1 + c <= 2p-2 there also avoids redundantly carrying c = p-1 into the subsequent paragraph.
Page 5, Lemma 2.2(b): The arithmetic pairing lemma is proved cleanly but never explicitly referenced elsewhere in the paper (its mechanism is restated inline inside Lemma 4.2).
strong_novelty_candidates: Strict separation D(H_{p^3}) <= 4p-4 < 4p-3 = L(H_{p^3}) for all odd primes p >= 3 and conceptual proof of D(H_27) = 8.
Three-set pigeonhole splitting criterion on the central fiber Z(H_{p^3}) (Lemma 2.2(d)) combined with heavy-line elimination (Lemma 4.1) and Property-B cross-splitting (Lemma 4.2).
Exact structural reduction of the remaining [3p, 4p-4] interval for p >= 5 to obstructions (O1)-(O2) (Theorem 1.2).
Fiber-doubled lifting witnesses T_eta and T_s establishing eta(H_{p^3}) >= 7p-6 and s(H_{p^3}) >= 8p-7 for all odd primes p >= 3 (Theorem 1.3).
